subject: Dedicated fleet margining and SKU recommendation for Zephyr Health
messages:

Subject: Dedicated fleet margining and SKU recommendation for Zephyr Health

Hi team / Alyssa,

Following our discovery, I sketched a Dedicated fleet plan for Zephyr's production workload (attached). High level options below — aim is to balance latency SLOs, embedding throughput, and cost predictability. I want internal alignment before we formalize a quote.

Option A — H100-first (high-memory, high perf)
- Use H100 80GB for primary serving for models with long context (>32k) and production embedding workloads.
- Pros: single-SKU simplicity, best latency for large contexts, fewer fallback conversions.
- Cons: highest unit cost; may be overprovisioned for routine short-context calls.

Option B — A100 primary with H100 burst
- A100 40GB reserved pool for day-to-day throughput (chat + short context generation), reserved H100 pool for embedding jobs and long-context fallbacks.
- Pros: better cost-per-token for typical traffic, preserves H100 where memory matters.
- Cons: added routing complexity and KV cache compatibility considerations.

Option C — A mixed approach (A100 + L4 tier for cost-sensitive low-memory paths)
- A100 baseline; L4 instances for stateless, lower-cost document parsing / high-QPS short responses; H100 reserved only for embedding transforms and long-LRU contexts.
- Pros: lowest blended unit cost; good for bursty workloads.
- Cons: model variants and quantization needed; careful eval required to avoid regressions.

Recommendations (internal):
1) Target A100 primary with a small H100 reserve for embeddings and long-context requests.
2) Add a 20% capacity margin for headroom at peak and to accommodate KV cache persistence.
3) Use L4 for non-SLO-critical, high-QPS endpoints to lower cost.
4) Propose 12-month reserved commit to hit Zephyr's desired pricing band; include hosted burst as a fallback for unexpected spikes.

Attachments: zephyr_capacity_model.xlsx (workbook with traffic scenarios) and zephyr_pricing_deck_v1.pdf (proposed pricing bands).

Alyssa — could you confirm: a) your 99th pctl latency SLO target, b) monthly token budget range, and c) whether embeddings will be batched overnight or in real time? Answering these will let us size the H100 reserve precisely.

Thanks,
Marissa

Picking up the technical sizing:
- Memory tradeoffs: H100 (80GB) vs A100 (40GB) vs L4 (24GB). Real-world constraints: models with long KV caches and >32k context need H100 to avoid frequent evictions.
- Throughput: A100 shows ~1.6x cost-efficiency vs H100 for short-context generation in our benchmarks (same precision), but H100 is ~2-3x faster when context length grows and when using FP16 kernels optimized for H100.
- Quantization: L4 and A100 both benefit from int8 or int4 paths; recommend a compatibility test to ensure quality doesn't regress on the customer prompts.
- KV cache sizing: recommend reserving ~12GB per serving shard for high-concurrency interactive endpoints when supporting 8k-16k contexts. That affects how many models/shards fit per GPU.
- Autoscaling/bursting: enable hosted bursting for unpredictable spikes (cheap short-term capacity). For Dedicated, include a 20% baseline margin in the SLO calculation.

Operational notes:
- Model variants: ship a memory-optimized variant (quantized for A100) and a high-memory variant on H100. Router will fallback transparently based on request headers (context_length, endpoint tag).
- Migration: we can start with a 50/20/30 split (A100 / H100 / L4) in the cap model for the first 3 months and iterate after observing traffic.

I ran quick numbers in the attached workbook; happy to walk through the math with the team.

-Dev
